newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein defends condolence trip to Israel.
newsitem.headline: King Hussein defends condolence trip to Israel.

text.p: King Hussein of Jordan hit out on Wednesday at opponents who criticised his trip to Israel in March to console relatives of seven Israeli schoolgirls shot dead by a Jordanian soldier.
The king told senior military officers in a speech broadcast on Jordanian television that his visit, when he kneeled next to grieving Israeli families, was a humanitarian duty.

He was responding to criticism both at home and in the Arab world that Jordan's reaction to the shooting showed more concern for a handful of Israeli victims than for Arabs killed in conflict with the Jewish state.
Jordan and Israel signed a peace treaty in 1994 ending a 46-year state of war, but popular hostility to Israel remains.

"From a humanitarian point of view if any one of you had seen the scenes that I had seen and was as pained as I was -- one bows one's head to anyone and any family, irrespective of who they are," the king said.
Opposition figures in Jordan criticised the government for "begging forgiveness" for the March shooting of the schoolgirls, saying Israel had never apologised for the deaths of Arabs.

Lebanese President Elias Hrawi accused King Hussein of caring more for the seven Israelis than for more than 100 Lebanese civilians killed when Israel shelled a U.N. base in the south Lebanese village of Qana.
"The president of a brotherly state whom we love...said why didn't (the king) do something like this in Qana?" King Hussein said. "By God what we did in Qana, was as much as anyone else."
